context: GitHub-hosted runners currently fail before any workflow step, so DIG relies on local/Qube QA as supplemental evidence. The prior local QA report embedded complete stdout/stderr for every shard, creating unbounded artifact growth and avoidable secret exposure.

reviews.reason: Preserves proof that exact output existed while retaining enough diagnostics for failed shards.
Successful shards do not need raw logs in durable evidence; failed diagnostics are redacted for common private keys, GitHub/OpenAI-style tokens, authorization values, passwords and secrets.
Keeps report size bounded with negligible CPU/memory cost and changes only evidence serialization, not worker/runtime semantics.

alternatives.name: store-complete-output
alternatives.rejected: Unbounded artifact size and highest secret-leak risk.

alternatives.name: store-output-hashes-only
alternatives.rejected: Best confidentiality but too weak for diagnosing local/Qube failures while hosted CI is unavailable.

alternatives.name: bounded-redacted-diagnostic-evidence
alternatives.tradeoffs: Heuristic redaction cannot prove every secret format is removed, so failed diagnostic tails remain supplemental and should not contain intentionally sensitive test data.

qa: successful shards store byte count and SHA-256 only
failed shards store byte count, SHA-256 and at most 4096 bytes of redacted tail
large successful output is not embedded
dirty worktree, SHA mismatch and timeout remain fail-closed
lessons: QA evidence is itself a security boundary and must have an explicit output policy.
Debuggability should be bounded independently from proof-of-execution; hashes preserve integrity evidence without retaining all logs.
Local QA remains supplemental and does not replace independent hosted CI or real Qubes qualification.
